extracted.intended_audience: literary scholars, editors, and readers of historical Hungarian correspondence (Mikes Kelemen)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and preparing a historical letters collection for publication: judging authenticity, textual fidelity, literary value, and historical usefulness of the correspondence and the editor's interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity / genuineness of correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: „Jogosúlt azon kétség, mely a levelek – mint olyanok – ellen emeltetik." (The legitimate doubt raised about the letters as genuine correspondence.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate provenance and plausibility of purported correspondents (e.g., the claimed 'nénje' in Constantinople). Check for anachronisms, omissions (e.g., absence of expected mentions such as the correspondent's husband), and implausible patterns (letters attributed to a nearby relative while the author reports being in the same city). Use internal inconsistencies and external evidence to judge whether items are true spontaneous letters or later constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency and unified design
rubrics_metrics.description: „Egy tervszerű egészet látunk magunk előtt... de azonegy hangulat sugallata alatt, valódi műszándékból, készűlt." (Whether the collection reads like a purposefully planned whole or merely a grab-bag of disparate letters.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether there is coherent development in views, feelings and expression across the corpus (evidence of an 'inner development'). Distinguish a genuinely organic series of letters from material later arranged into an artificial unity or from a deliberate 'memoir' assembled from papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plausibility of informational access and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions about how the author could know certain 'fővárosi' events or how quickly European news reached Constantinople given slow post (e.g., "mint tudhatá meg az európai eseményeket sokszor 8–10 nap alatt...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check temporal plausibility: intervals between events and reported dates; whether the speed of news transmission in the period makes the reports credible; and whether detailed local knowledge attributed to a remote correspondent is plausible. Implausible rapid reporting or access to insider details may indicate later compilation, interpolation, or forgery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency and topical distribution of letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation that on some subjects (e.g., the Turkish empire and religion between 1748–1752) there are only a few letters per year, which is atypical for regular correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare expected frequency of letters on major topics with actual distribution. Sparse or clustered topical coverage that departs from expected epistolary habits may signal selective compilation or editorial omission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of the letter form for certain kinds of material
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'levélalak' (letter form) tends to be less satisfactory for 'puszta leírást' or statistical/state description: "a választott levélalaknak tulajdonítandó... legkevésbbé azonban a puszta leírást."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating passages of descriptive/state/statistical content, consider whether the letter genre naturally accommodates sustained exposition. If not, judge whether the material reads as forced into epistolary form (sign of later redaction) or whether the author successfully adapts the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diary-immediacy vs constructed memoir voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument that Mikes likely kept a diary-like record ('Naplózott ő, kétségkivűl') and that many passages show the immediacy of a 'néma megbizottja' rather than contrived correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess immediacy of impressions, presence of minute/point-in-time details, spontaneity of feeling and perception; these support diary or live-letter status. Conversely, polished, reflective, or harmonized prose may indicate later memoir-like revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary qualities: tone, humor, memory and erudition
rubrics_metrics.description: Positive evaluation criteria: conveys feelings and moods, 'józan itéletét s előrelátó bölcseségét', frequent humor and anecdote, extensive reading and apt allusions ('Eleven emlékezetéből... a történelem, az anekdotonok gyöngyeit').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge stylistic features: clarity of judgment, balance of humor and pathos, anecdotal richness, classical/foreign-literary references, and use of memory. These qualities support high literary merit and enduring interest across ages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical/informational value for historians and statisticians
rubrics_metrics.description: The part 'a török birodalom ismertetése' is singled out as especially valuable to the statistician/historian ('azon rész, mely a statisticusra nézve legbecsesb').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate factual content for detail, specificity, accuracy and usefulness: descriptions of institutions, customs, events, and administrative matters. Cross-check with other contemporary sources. Rate the material's utility for historians of the Ottoman Empire and comparative studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of editorial intervention and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial choices matter: this edition presents the work 'teljesben, mint Kulcsár, egy szakaszszal, s hívebben, mert Kulcsár változtatásai nélkül' — decisions about following earlier editors or restoring original readings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and evaluate what the editor kept, altered, or omitted compared to earlier editions. Justify choices (faithfulness vs modernization). Indicate where sections were added, excised, or reordered, and assess how selection affects interpretation of the author's intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcription principles: preserve original orthography vs normalize
rubrics_metrics.description: Stated policy: 'Az eredeti szöveg helyesírásán nem változtattunk. A nyomdai hibákat javítottuk.' (Do not change original spelling; correct typographical errors.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt and state a clear transcription protocol: keep author's orthography and dialectal forms to preserve voice, but correct obvious printer's errors; supply an explicit list of emendations and corrections. Provide a transcriber's note explaining conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial apparatus: footnotes, references and emendation lists
rubrics_metrics.description: This edition supplies extensive footnotes cross-referencing letters and sources and a list of 'Javítások' and 'Transcriber's note' enumerating corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide thorough scholarly apparatus: numbered footnotes citing letter numbers/pages, references to external sources, explanatory notes for historical/contextual items, and a clear emendation/corrections list. This supports verifiability and scholarly use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherent endpoint / completeness of the edition
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor argues that the material naturally ends around Zay's death in 1758 and that this 'momentum maga fejezheté be kerekdeden a művet.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide and justify editorially on the work's proper endpoint: whether to present up to a clear concluding moment that forms a satisfying whole, or to include additional fragmentary material. Ensure choices are argued and signaled to readers.
